The edit's exact rules: (1) MACHINE RESULT (T5-01): a verification entry carries a machine result only through exit (an int that is not a bool), counts (a dict whose checks, passed and failed are ints where present; a None member is absent) or output_sha256 (64 hex); a non-int exit, or a counts member that is neither an int nor None, is REFUSED with its own reason. An entry is BOUND only when it is a machine result, names a tool, has artifact_sha256_at_run equal to the live digest AND is PASSING: exit == 0 when exit is present; failed == 0 when failed is present; passed == checks when both are present; and its verdict, when present, does not start (after strip and casefold) with 'red', 'fail' or 'refus'. A bound-but-failing entry yields the reason 'verification[i] is bound to the shipped bytes and FAILED' and does not count toward bound. (2) CHECKER VERDICT (T5-01): the distinct_checker verdict, casefolded, must match ACCEPT = \b(fit_to_accept|fit_with_changes|confirmed|accept(?:ed|able)?)\b by CONTAINMENT and must not match REFUSE = \b(not_fit|not fit|unfit|refut\w*|reject\w*|blocker\w*|red)\b; a verdict matching neither, or both, is REFUSED.
